paragraphs: Friend, here's what sits heavy on me about this one. Samson had been strong for so long that he figured the strength was just HIS. Look at the end of the story. He wakes up, thinks, "I will escape as I did before and shake myself free," and the Bible says, "But he did not know that the LORD had departed from him." (Judges 16:20)

Now watch how it got there. Delilah pressed him daily, and the text says she pleaded "until he was sick to death." (Judges 16:16) Three times he gave her a fake answer, and every time the Philistines were that much closer to his bedroom door. I think that's the lesson, baker: a little pressure we keep brushing off can wear us down until we hand over something God told us to guard. Samson told her about his Nazirite hair, the sign he had been set apart to God from his mother's womb (Judges 16:17), and that's when everything unraveled.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery today. Our strength is never ours to run on autopilot, and the real danger is not noticing when we've drifted from the Lord. It hurts to see Samson in that prison, but hold onto this one small line: "the hair of his head began to grow back after it had been shaved." (Judges 16:22) His story isn't over, friend, and neither is God's.
